intro: The property pack, for letting and managing buildings and estates: properties, units and their owners, leases with rent and deposits, the rent roll and landlords' statements, inspections, tenants' repairs and owners' levies. Switch the pack on in Organisation › Settings › Industry packs, at the places you manage.
start: Turn the property pack on in Organisation › Settings › Industry packs.
Add your owners, then each property and its units, on Properties and units.
Make a lease for each let unit and sign it. Its rent falls due on its own from then.
Check the rent roll each month and record payments as they come in.

articles.title: Add a property, its units and their owner
articles.summary: Record who owns the units and how they are paid, then the building and each unit in it with its asking rent.

steps.rest: Choose the customer who owns the units and, if you pay them out, their supplier account. Set their fee and how much a repair may cost before they must say yes, then press Add the owner.
give it a name, kind, area and address, and press Add the property.
for each flat, shop or office. Enter its bedrooms, floor, asking rent and how often rent is paid, and choose its owner.
It shows as vacant until a lease is signed.

tips: For an estate that charges levies by share, fill in each unit's share of the estate.
Choose Take off the market from a unit's actions while it cannot be let, and Put back on the market when it can.

articles.title: Make a lease and sign it
articles.summary: Choose the unit and the tenant, set the term and rent, sign the lease and record the caution deposit.

steps.rest: when it starts and ends, the rent a period and whether it is paid a month, a quarter or a year, the caution deposit, the agency fee and the notice.

articles.summary: Remind the tenant, offer a new term with any rise, and turn an acceptance into the next lease. Or record notice and end it.

articles.title: Invoice the rent and record payments
articles.summary: See what fell due this month and who is late, invoice the month's rent and record each payment.

steps.rest: and choose the month. Who owes, by how late shows what is late and by how many days.

articles.title: Send a landlord their monthly statement
articles.summary: Show the rent you collected for their units, less your fee and repairs, and the payout you owe them.

steps.lead: Under A landlord's statement, choose the landlord
steps.rest: and press Show the statement.

steps.lead: Check the rent received and the repairs.
steps.rest: The fee and the payout are worked out.
The payout is billed to the landlord's supplier account, ready to pay.

articles.title: Inspect a unit and settle the deposit
articles.summary: Book a move-in, routine or move-out inspection, go room by room, take any deductions from the deposit and refund the rest.

steps.rest: Choose the unit, the kind, when and the inspector, and press Book it.
For each item, choose how it is now (good, fair, damaged or missing), add a note, and press Save the rooms. Anything worse than last time is flagged.

steps.lead: At a move-out, add each deduction
steps.rest: with the amount, why and a photo that shows it, and press Take it from the deposit.
The tenant is sent the report and may answer within the days your settings allow.
then press Settle the deposit. The rest is refunded.

tips: Deductions can only be made at a move-out inspection, and each needs a reason and a photo.

articles.title: Handle a tenant's repair request
articles.summary: Log the problem, give it to a contractor with the cost and who pays, get the owner's yes where needed, and mark it done.

steps.rest: Say where it is and what is wrong, how urgent it is, how it came in and who reported it. Press Log the request.
from its actions. Enter the contractor, when they are booked, the cost and who pays: the tenant, the landlord or the owners' fund. Press Assign it.

steps.lead: If it waits for the owner,
steps.rest: choose The owner says yes or The owner says no once they answer.

enter the final cost and press It is done. The tenant is invoiced, the landlord's statement takes it off, or the owners' budget pays it.

tips: A repair the landlord or the owners' fund pays waits for the owner's yes when it costs more than their limit.

articles.title: Set an estate's budget and raise the owners' levy
articles.summary: Agree the year's budget and how it is shared, raise the levy on each owner, record what they pay and what is spent.

steps.rest: choose the year and how the levy is shared (equal for every unit, by floor area, or by each unit's share), add the budget lines and press Make the budget.
once the owners agree it.
choose the period, what it raises and when it is due, and press Raise the levy. Each owner is charged their part.

tips: A levy can only be raised on an approved budget, and only once a period.
Spending can never go past a line, nor past what the levy has collected.
